dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Before writing code, systematically read README, helpers.py (multiple ranges), conftest, run.sh, and every public test file plus oracle_fixtures — comprehensive extraction of the client-touched contract surface.
Deliberate library selection (FastAPI/uvicorn for built-in WS, openpyxl for xlsx) after checking installed packages — a considered I/O/eval-library decision.
Reconciled the workbook summary envelope ambiguity (sheets as names on create vs. objects-with-cells on full GET) directly from observed test assertions — contract-driven correction.
Re-consulted the contract when reaching the xlsx subsystem (round-trip test for named ranges, re-read spec on CF/DV round-trip) rather than assuming — re-orientation as new subsystems were reached.

Excel semantics (LOG base, SUM("3"), TEXT percent, STDEV.S) reasoned from memory and validated against dev tests/oracle fixtures rather than probed against an independent LibreOffice oracle; several tricky areas (cycle, LAMBDA, tokenizer) surfaced reactively via test failures.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went well beyond a skim (anchor 3): it read helpers.py, run.sh, and the entire public test suite plus oracle fixtures up front, chose libraries deliberately, and formed a working model of the full cell/formula/collab contract (anchor 5+). It also reconciled ambiguities from observed client behavior (step 53) and re-consulted the contract/oracle at new subsystems like xlsx (steps 104-106), which are level-8/10 traits. However, it never built a durable explicit contract map and grounded Excel semantics largely from memory rather than probing a LibreOffice oracle, with much tricky-area understanding emerging reactively from dev-test failures — keeping it short of a full 8, landing at 7.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: After reading the contract, the agent lays out design decisions and a module build order (parser → evaluator → functions → workbook → store → server → xlsx) that follows the real dependency chain — more than a flat to-do list, but stated as prose rather than an explicit milestone hierarchy with done-criteria.

The agent built the entire ~150-function engine breadth before ever standing up the server/health/persistence loop, contrary to anchor-8's 'get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core round-trip green before breadth' — breadth was front-loaded ahead of the load-bearing skeleton.
Uses the runnable dev suite as a concrete done-check at a checkpoint ('123/131 passing'), tying progress to verifiable test results — a rough-checkpoint pattern between anchors 5 and 8.

Once all 131 smoke tests are green, deliberately re-orients into a distinct hidden-suite hardening phase (performance, persistence, xlsx round-trip, edge cases), showing some staged re-sequencing rather than a single undifferentiated push.

Hardening phase proceeds as a sensible sequence of targeted probes with implicit pass/fail checks, but the ordering is reactive and the per-item plans stay tactical rather than a living, risk-ranked milestone plan (short of anchor 10).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly phases the work into dependency-ordered stages (contract → engine core → server/persistence → smoke-suite green → hidden-suite hardening) and repeatedly uses the runnable dev suite as done-checks at checkpoints, which is above the flat, unordered anchor-5 list. However, it never articulated an explicit milestone hierarchy with pre-declared done-criteria, and it front-loaded the full ~150-function breadth before proving a live-server/persistence/core round-trip skeleton green — the specific pattern anchor 8 requires. That places it between 5 and 8, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Read the oracle_fixtures (basic_arithmetic.json, aggregates.json) — grounding expected values in the Excel/LibreOffice ground-truth corpus rather than only the smoke tests.
Runs dev_tests/run.sh repeatedly as a baseline (123/131 → 131/131), but treats it as a floor not the finish line.

Built its own performance probes explicitly against the stated ceilings: 1000-cell linear chain, 5000 dependents, and 100k-cell import (measured 5.5s vs 30s bound) — benchmarking the performance ceilings.
Self-built xlsx round-trip tests via openpyxl including named ranges, then extended to CF/DV export/import round-trip fidelity — beyond what the smoke suite covers.

Numerous targeted python3 probes for function correctness (DEC2HEX tokenizer bug, LAMBDA/LET-bound lambdas, COUNTIF wildcards, ghost-cell spill refs, boolean serialization, display formatting) with each failure driving a specific fix.
Explicitly tested persistence across process restart and next_id counter survival — a spec-mandated property not fully exercised by run.sh.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes well beyond running the smoke suite: it grounds some expected values in the provided oracle fixtures, builds its own performance probes against the stated ceilings, round-trips xlsx (incl. named ranges/CF/DV) through openpyxl, exercises error/spill edge cases, and consistently uses failures to drive fixes — the textbook level-8 behavior. It falls short of 10 because verification is ad-hoc one-off scripting rather than a systematic reusable harness, oracle grounding is partial, and several subsystems (collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek) are only exercised via the smoke suite rather than self-built probes.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: Identifies exact failing tests from the 123/131 result, tracks the remaining count down individually (LAMBDA, xlsx import, map/reduce), and makes distinct forward progress each debugging pass rather than looping — no circular re-debugging.
Promptly detects stuck states (infinite-loop hangs) and interrupts to investigate rather than waiting or retrying blindly.

Repeated surface-wide enumerations of what's still missing (functions like IFERROR/DATEDIF/DOLLAR, xlsx CF/DV round-trip, 100k-cell perf, persistence, E2E) sustained across the whole horizon — but as periodic mental spot-checks, not a maintained ledger.
Uses the 131-test pass count as the running source of truth, re-running after each change to confirm no regressions — tracking reconciled against verification, not self-report.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent tracks progress against actual verification results (dev-test pass counts) and repeatedly scans the whole feature surface for gaps, while promptly catching infinite-loop stalls and avoiding circular re-debugging — clearly above anchor 5's 'checklist of major features.' But it never maintains an explicit granular ledger of the function catalog or endpoint families with done/partial/not-started status; its tracking is implicit and driven mostly by the smoke-suite count plus periodic mental enumerations, falling short of anchor 8's live granular ledger. This lands at a 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Recognized LET parsing was structurally wrong and rewrote the parse strategy (parse args generically then transform) rather than patching the buggy loop.

Deps 4/7 failing; traced cycle-detection failure to deps not being recorded before recompute, then reworked the dependency-graph model with static ref-extraction pre-recording — a design revision addressing the root assumption.
xlsx import formulas evaluating to 0; diagnosed as import-ordering assumption (formulas reference later-added cells) and reworked to import-all-then-recompute in both workbook and store loader.
LET-bound lambda invoked by name returned #NAME?; diagnosed parser producing Call(TRIPLE) instead of Apply, revised _eval_call dispatch to consult env bindings.
DEC2HEX returned None; root-caused to tokenizer regex ordering rather than assuming a missing function.

After dev tests green, proactively verified restart persistence, 1000-cell chain, 5000-dependent propagation, and 100k-cell import against the stated perf budgets, and re-ran full suite after each change to avoid regressions.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the build the agent repeatedly treated failing/surprising signals as evidence of wrong underlying assumptions — dependency-graph recording order, xlsx import sequencing, lambda dispatch, tokenizer regex order — and reworked the relevant design rather than piling on local patches, re-verifying with the full suite each time without derailing other subsystems (anchor 8). It stops short of 10 because most divergences were surfaced reactively by the provided smoke suite rather than detected early via self-built verification, though the later proactive performance/persistence probing shows genuine forward-looking steering.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Built the function library breadth-first across every catalog family (math, trig, aggregates, statistics, text, distributions, financial, date/time, info, lookup, dynamic-array, engineering, database) rather than deep-diving one — securing broad working coverage first.

Systematically implemented all endpoint families (cells, sheets, fill, sort, filter, csv, xlsx, names, settings, validation, conditional_formats, pivot, goal_seek, websocket) as a breadth sweep, covering the full graded surface.

After dev tests passed, explicitly reasoned about maximizing the hidden suite: '200 formula corpus', and added commonly-reached functions likely to appear (RAND, IFERROR, DATEDIF, etc.) — conscious targeting of graded return, not arbitrary polish.

Consciously timeboxed low-yield depth: OFFSET ('For now, let me implement...') and OOXML conditional-format export ('CF in OOXML is complex. Let me try to do basic support'), deferring exhaustive edge work.

Revisited allocation post-green — weighing display formatting, xlsx round-trip, percentage/boolean edge cases — but the second-phase additions were somewhat opportunistic rather than a systematic catalog-gap reallocation, keeping it short of a full 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent secured broad working coverage of the entire function catalog and endpoint surface before any edge-case depth, then explicitly reasoned about hidden-suite graded return and consciously timeboxed low-yield niches (OOXML CF, OFFSET) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It did revisit allocation after dev tests passed, but the reallocation was more opportunistic than a systematic, gap-analysis-driven strategy, so it falls short of the deliberate revisited allocation described at 10.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
